findings.title: realGuide smoke test depends on the committed guide checkout, which the repo may have trimmed
findings.description: Description: `INSTALLED_GUIDE` is hardcoded to `REPO_ROOT/project-documents/ai-project-guide/project-guides` (the guide committed into this repo, not a fixture). Two consequences: (1) the test breaks whenever that committed guide's rules or layout change — its own header admits "real rules change often", so it is the most drift-sensitive test in the suite; (2) it requires the committed guide to be complete: I verified this repo's committed guide has `project-guides/lint` but no `lint/python/ruff.toml`, so if any language's lint source files are ever excluded/trimmed in the committed copy, `checkLintConfigs`/`writeOrSuggest` will throw `ENOENT`, which `installIde` does not classify (only `InstallAbort` and `errno`-coded fs errors from the install itself are converted to exit 1), turning the smoke test into a hard crash. Consider pinning the test to a small dedicated fixture or skipping with an explicit message when the installed guide is incomplete.

findings.title: readRulesExclude throws a plain Error the installer's catch does not classify
findings.description: Description: `readRulesExclude` throws `new Error('rules.exclude resolved to a ...')` when the config value is not a string. It is awaited inside `installCheckout`, so the throw happens *before* `installIde`'s try block: for the root install it propagates as an unexpected `Error` (prints "Error: rules.exclude resolved to...", exit 1), but the documented contract in `installWorktrees` — "A worktree whose install fails (exit 1, which includes filesystem errors) is recorded and the loop continues; any other exception is a bug and propagates" — classifies a malformed per-worktree config value as "a bug" that aborts the remaining worktrees. A malformed `rules.exclude` in one worktree's config is a user-config problem, not an install bug; wrapping it in `UserError` (or having `installIde` classify it) would keep the fail-continue behavior the comment promises. The normal path is well-tested; this error path is untested.

findings.title: realGuide test uses a loose string-keyed record for the target dimension
findings.description: Description: `const EXPECTED: Record<string, string[]>` accepts any string target, so a typo in a key (e.g. `'claud'`) would silently add a new, always-passing target via `it.each(Object.keys(EXPECTED))` and never exercise the installer. The canonical set is already typed as `Target` in `commands/ideTargets.ts`; typing this as `Record<Target, string[]>` makes the four-target coverage compiler-enforced, matching the "one definition per target" pattern used for `TARGETS` and `TARGET_SETUP` in the source under review.

findings.title: Verified: worktree loop, dry-run sandbox, and lint port are correct and tested at the right seams
findings.description: Description: Confirmed against the underlying files: `propagationTargets` filters out non-existent paths and the root-path default worktree (so `wt.worktreePath!` is safe), `installWorktrees` uses `installCheckout` for both root and worktrees with per-checkout `rules.exclude`, and the exit-1/propagate split matches the error boundary in `installer.ts` (`InstallAbort` → exit 1, errno-coded fs error → exit 1, else propagate). Dry-run: sandbox created via `mkdtemp`, `INSTALL_PATHS` copied with the `.claude/worktrees` skip, install run with `targetRoot` swapped, stdout replayed through `DRY_RUN_KEEP`, and `rmSync` in `finally` (leaked-sandbox regression pinned by `flags.test.ts`'s "removes the dry-run sandbox when the install aborts"). Lint port: `missingRequirements`/`alternatives` match `lint_missing_requirements` including the `while read` final-line quirk, `findDotnetProjects` matches the `find -maxdepth 3` prune expression, and the layered-ruff path matches `lint_check_python`. Tests are organized per convention (centralized `tests/`, `describe.each` over targets, behavior-level assertions in `setup-ide.test.ts` pinning only what cf passes to the mocked installer, real-tmp-dir integration in `tests/ideInstall`). No action needed; listed so the PASS rests on inspection, not on the diff hunks.
